title: All three offices locked out of Teams sign-in from mid-morning
scenario: Everyone at a food producer loses Teams sign-in at once; the customer's own resolver and proxy checks come back clean, service health shows an active Microsoft incident, and the failures stop when it is restored.

events.title: TEAMS SIGN-IN DOWN EVERYWHERE
events.text:
Teams sign-in is dead for the whole company since about 10:20. 200+ people, all three offices, nobody can get in. Our CEO is standing next to me. Is this something on our side?? Please call back if you need to.

Ola Brandvold, Tallgrass Foods

events.title: Priority raised
events.text: Priority raised from P3 to P1 automatically: affected-user estimate above 100 (keyword match). Duty manager notified.

events.title: Service health check
events.text: 10:40 UTC: opened Microsoft 365 service health. Active incident TM502817, 'Teams sign-ins failing or slow for customers in Europe', start 10:12 UTC, status investigating. Message center has nothing else relevant. This matches the customer's symptoms and timing.

events.title: There is a Microsoft incident
events.text:
Hi Ola, there is an active Microsoft incident (TM502817) for Teams sign-in in Europe that began at 10:12 UTC, which fits what you're seeing. There's nothing you need to change on your side. I'll check the incident every 30 minutes and email you with each change; you'll hear from me by 12:30 UTC at the latest.

Priya

events.title: Our own checks
events.text:
Ola asked me to rule out our side. I queried login.microsoftonline.com and the CDN name on each of our three resolvers (10.20.0.2, .3, .4) with Resolve-DnsName: every answer correct, about 20 ms. I also pushed the same requests through both proxy nodes and both answer normally. Looks like it's not our DNS or proxy.

Karl (network)

events.title: is it just me?
events.text: is it just me or is everyone down?? Edge shows ERR_CONNECTION_TIMED_OUT every time i press sign in. i have tried 6 times. i have a client call at 11:30 pls help

events.title: Incident update: service restored
events.text:
Hi Ola, I looked at the incident page again just now: Microsoft has posted TM502817 as service restored at 11:58 UTC (cause given: a faulty configuration change in the regional sign-in front door). Please ask a handful of people across the three offices to sign in and tell me if anyone still fails. I'll keep the case open until tomorrow 09:00 UTC.

Priya

events.title: Re: Incident update: service restored
events.text: All three offices are back in. About 200 people have been signing in since noon with no trouble. Thanks for the quick answer.

events.title: Case closed
events.text: Status changed from Waiting on customer to Closed. Reason: no further contact for 24 hours.
